frozen_candidate_root_contribution: A deficit/breach in self-sufficient wholeness — the root marks a subject (or the infliction) of being broken below the level of complete, standing sufficiency, i.e. lacking the resource/integrity needed to stand on one's own. In the participant/state family (faqīr, fuqarāʾ, faqr) this surfaces as "one/state characterized by a shortfall of means → needy, destitute"; in the event family (fāqira) it surfaces as "an event that ruptures wholeness → a shattering, back-breaking blow." The root supplies the DEFICIT/RUPTURE-OF-WHOLENESS pole, never the sufficiency itself.

In the participant/state family (faqīr, fuqarāʾ, faqr) this surfaces as "one/state characterized by a shortfall of means → needy, destitute"; in the event family (fāqira) it surfaces as "an event that ruptures wholeness → a shattering, back-breaking blow." internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Two form-families exhaust the data. FAMILY A — the faqīr/fuqarāʾ/faqr cluster (13 of 14) — is anchored internally by its repeated, explicit opposition to ghinā/ghaniyy (self-sufficiency/wealth), which makes the residue "shortfall of sufficient means" surface-recoverable: 3:181 quotes the disbelievers "inna llāha faqīrun wa-naḥnu aghniyāʾ" (God is faqīr, we are rich) — faqīr = ascribed a deficit set against aghniyāʾ; 4:135 "in yakun ghaniyyan aw faqīran" and 4:6 "wa-man kāna ghaniyyan… wa-man kāna faqīran" pair the two poles directly; 35:15 "antumu l-fuqarāʾu ilā llāhi wa-llāhu huwa l-ghaniyy" and 47:38 "wa-llāhu l-ghaniyyu wa-antumu l-fuqarāʾ" set human deficit against divine sufficiency. The alms verses designate the faqīr as the licensed recipient precisely because he is in deficit: 9:60 "innamā l-ṣadaqātu lil-fuqarāʾi wa-l-masākīn…", 2:271, 2:273 "lil-fuqarāʾi lladhīna uḥṣirū fī sabīli llāh", 59:8 "lil-fuqarāʾi l-muhājirīn", 22:28 "wa-aṭʿimū l-bāʾisa l-faqīr". 24:32 "in yakūnū fuqarāʾa yughnihimu llāhu min faḍlih" is decisive: the state fqr is the very thing removed by God making them ghaniyy (yughni-him). 2:268 "al-shayṭānu yaʿidukumu l-faqra" abstracts the same as the state-noun (poverty). 28:24 "innī limā anzalta ilayya min khayrin faqīr" = "I am in deficit of / in need of whatever good You send me" — with the construction ilā/li supplying the directed-dependency vector, the root itself still contributes only the deficit. FAMILY B — fāqira (75:25) "taẓunnu an yufʿala bihā fāqiratun" — an event done TO the gloomy faces: a back-breaking calamity. Subtracting the fāʿila event-noun morphology, the residue is the same deficit/breach, now realized as an act that ruptures a subject's wholeness rather than a standing state of lack. Across both families the invariant left after removing morphology, construction, participants and context is: a breach/deficit of self-sufficient wholeness.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: (a) FORM: ADJ/N faqīr = "one characterized by [deficit]"; plural fuqarāʾ = plurality of same; verbal-noun faqr (2:268) = "the state of [deficit]"; fāʿila fāqira (75:25) = "an event that enacts [rupture]". Stripping these leaves the bare deficit/rupture notion. (b) CONSTRUCTION: ilā in 35:15 and li/ilā in 28:24 supply the DIRECTED-DEPENDENCY vector ("in need TOWARD X"); the li- frame in 9:60/2:271/2:273/59:8 supplies RECIPIENT-DESIGNATION for alms; the overt ghaniyy/ghinā antonym frame supplies the sufficiency-pole against which the deficit is read. The root does not contribute the direction or the beneficiary-assignment — only the deficit that motivates them. (c) PARTICIPANTS: God (falsely, 3:181; as sufficiency-pole 35:15/47:38), orphans (4:6), witnesses (4:135), muhājirūn (59:8), destitute pilgrims (2:273), humankind (35:15) — the residue is participant-independent. (d) CONTEXT: alms-law (9:60, 2:271, 2:273), marriage/provision (24:32), narrative (28:24), theological polemic (3:181, 35:15, 47:38), eschatology (75:25). After subtracting all four layers the constant is a breach/deficit of self-sufficient wholeness.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 75:25:5:1 (fāqira). It is the single occurrence outside the poverty/need cluster: "taẓunnu an yufʿala bihā fāqiratun" describes a back-breaking calamity inflicted on the gloomy faces, not a state of material lack. It reconciles by reading the fāʿila event-noun morphology over the same root deficit: fāqira = an act that RUPTURES a subject's wholeness/integrity (breaks the back), which is the event-side of the very "breach of self-sufficient wholeness" that, on the state-side, yields faqīr = one whose means are broken below sufficiency. The reconciliation is genuine but INFERENTIAL: with only one fāqira token and no internal verse bridging "breaking" to "lack", the shared "rupture-of-wholeness" center is recovered by abstraction from the form, not demonstrated by an attested internal link. Hence unity holds here but at the abstract altitude, not the surface.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The strongest alternative is the narrower residue "NEED/LACK OF MATERIAL RESOURCES (poverty)". It covers 13 of 14 occurrences more crisply than the abstract formulation — the ghaniyy-opposition, the alms-recipient designation, and yughnihimu llāh in 24:32 all read most naturally as economic poverty. Internal evidence arbitrates against it, however: fāqira (75:25) is a calamity, not poverty, so "poverty" cannot be the root residue without leaving 75:25 as an anomaly. The presence of fāqira forces the conceptual center up one level — from "material lack" to "deficit/rupture of self-sufficient wholeness" — of which poverty is the economic instantiation and the back-breaking blow is the event instantiation. So "poverty" is a form-and-context-bound surface reading of a more abstract root residue, not the residue itself.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest neighbors: (1) gh-n-y (ghinā/ghaniyy) — the direct ANTONYM (sufficiency/independence/wealth), co-present in 3:181, 4:6, 4:135, 24:32, 35:15, 47:38; fqr occupies the opposite, deficit pole. (2) s-k-n (miskīn) — a near-synonym for the destitute, listed DISTINCTLY beside fuqarāʾ in 9:60 ("lil-fuqarāʾi wa-l-masākīn"), which shows the language treats them as non-identical: skn contributes stillness/immobilized-lowliness of the poor, whereas fqr contributes the breach/deficit of self-sufficiency; the coordination proves they are not the same lexical residue. (3) k-s-r / calamity roots for fāqira — fqr is distinct in that its breach is specifically of WHOLENESS/standing-integrity (the back-breaking image), not generic breaking or destruction. Falsifiability: the residue fails if any occurrence used fqr for positive plenitude/abundance, or described a self-sufficient (ghaniyy) subject as faqīr in earnest, or used it for a want with no deficit located in the subject's own sufficiency. No occurrence does; 3:181 uses faqīr of God only inside a quoted false ascription, which the verse condemns — confirming, not violating, the deficit residue.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty residue — a deficit/breach of self-sufficient wholeness — is recoverable across all 14 occurrences after subtracting form, construction, participants and context, so the disposition is PREFERRED. Strength is MODERATE rather than STRONG for two honest reasons. First, the conceptual center is somewhat underdetermined between "material shortfall of means" (crisp for the 13 faqīr/fuqarāʾ/faqr tokens, anchored by the explicit ghinā antonym and by yughnihimu llāh in 24:32) and the more abstract "rupture of wholeness" needed to also cover fāqira; the 13 read most simply as poverty, and the abstract framing is imposed to secure unity with the one event-noun. Second, the sole hard case, fāqira (75:25), reconciles only by metaphorical/derivational extension (event-side rupture of wholeness), and that bridge between "back-breaking calamity" and "lack" is NOT internally attested — there is one fāqira token and no linking verse — so its recoverability rests on abstraction from morphology, not on internal demonstration. It is nonetheless genuinely reconcilable (not contradicted): the deficit/rupture notion is present, merely realized as an inflicted event rather than a standing state, so I do not force it into inconsistent_refs. Direction is determinate (fqr = the deficit pole, never sufficiency) and the root is sharply distinguished from its antonym gh-n-y and from co-listed s-k-n. The tension between a narrow, surface-crisp poverty sense and the abstract center required by fāqira is precisely what caps the strength at MODERATE.

adversarial_verification.notes: Refutation sweep of all 14. FAMILY A (13/14: 22:28, 24:32, 28:24, 2:268, 2:271, 2:273, 35:15, 3:181, 47:38, 4:135, 4:6, 59:8, 9:60) is robustly and INTERNALLY supported — the 'deficit of self-sufficient means' residue is recoverable from the text itself via explicit ghinā/ghaniyy antonymy (3:181, 4:135, 4:6, 35:15, 47:38) and the decisive removal-of-state construction in 24:32 (fuqarāʾ → yughnihimu llāh). Hardest Family-A case is 28:24 (Moses 'faqīr' for divine good), which edges toward generic dependency, but the ilā/li construction supplies the directed-dependency vector while the root contributes only the deficit — no failure. FAMILY B is the single problem: 75:25 fāqira ('back-breaking calamity') is an event-noun denoting a rupturing act done TO a subject, not a standing state of lack of means. The candidate bridges it via 'rupture of wholeness' (etymologically defensible: faqara = break the vertebrae, fiqār = spine), but this is the one seam not triangulable from the Quranic data: fāqira has no in-text antonym, co-member, or paraphrase, so its assignment to the same invariant rests on EXTERNAL etymology + morphological subtraction, and it forces the gloss to broaden from 'shortfall of means' to 'breach of integrity generally.' That is a genuine (if modest) over-breadth/underdetermination concern, hence PARTIALLY rather than SUPPORTED — not a contradiction, but saveable only by the etymological bridge. Neighbor-root contrast is clean: discriminates against ghny (explicit antonym, sufficiency pole) and against skn/miskīn (9:60 lists al-fuqarāʾ AND al-masākīn as distinct alms categories, so fqr does not collapse into generic destitution); vs generic need-roots (ḥwj/ʿwz) the 'self-sufficient wholeness' specificity is earned by the recurrent ghinā opposition. Falsifiable (failure = an occurrence meaning sufficiency or an unrelated sense; none present) and distinct.

occurrence_dispositions.note: al-faqīr paired with al-bāʾis as the licensed alms-recipient (wa-aṭʿimū l-bāʾisa l-faqīr); residue = one in shortfall of means → needy. Family A.
'in yakūnū fuqarāʾa yughnihimu llāhu' — the fqr state is precisely what God removes by making them ghaniyy; deficit pole explicit against ghinā.
'innī limā anzalta ilayya min khayrin faqīr' — li/ilā supplies directed dependency; root still contributes only the deficit/need residue.
al-faqr as state-noun 'poverty' promised by Satan; abstracted standing state of lack of sufficient means. Family A.
al-fuqarāʾ as designated recipients of ṣadaqāt precisely because in deficit; residue recoverable.
lil-fuqarāʾi lladhīna uḥṣirū… contrasted with yaḥsabuhum al-jāhilu aghniyāʾ — deficit set explicitly against ghinā.
'antumu l-fuqarāʾu ilā llāhi wa-llāhu huwa l-ghaniyy' — human deficit directly opposed to divine self-sufficiency.
disbelievers ascribe 'inna llāha faqīrun wa-naḥnu aghniyāʾ' — faqīr = ascribed deficit against aghniyāʾ; the ascription (though blasphemous) uses the deficit pole.
'wa-llāhu l-ghaniyyu wa-antumu l-fuqarāʾ' — human deficit against divine sufficiency, explicit ghinā/fqr opposition.
'in yakun ghaniyyan aw faqīran' — direct pairing of the two poles; faqīr = one in shortfall of means.
'wa-man kāna faqīran falyaʾkul bil-maʿrūf' vs 'ghaniyyan falyastaʿfif' — faqīr's deficit licenses drawing on the orphan's wealth; poles paired.
lil-fuqarāʾi l-muhājirīn who were driven from homes and property (ukhrijū min diyārihim wa-amwālihim) — deficit of means explicit in context.
Family B: fāqira as event done to the faces (yufʿalu bihā fāqiratun) — back-breaking calamity; subtracting fāʿila event-morphology leaves the breach/rupture-of-wholeness residue.
'innamā l-ṣadaqātu lil-fuqarāʾi wa-l-masākīn' — faqīr as deficit-bearing licensed recipient of alms.
